records.name: Kimi Code CLI
records.one_liner: Moonshot's TypeScript terminal coding agent: a 141k-LOC DI x Scope engine with an xstate turn loop (agent-core-v2), served through a pi-tui TUI, kimi -p stream-json, ACP, a Fastify REST/WS server, a VS Code extension and a remote-control relay; Kimi-first but neutral across four wire protocols.

dims.loop: An xstate turn machine (gating, thinking, retrying, acting, draining) inside an agent machine, wrapped by IAgentLoopService. Remote errors go through a recovery-proposal chain (credential refresh, media degradation) before Retry-After backoff. Queued prompts can be steered into the running turn. Hooks: onWillBeginStep, onDidFinishStep and ordered LoopErrorHandlers. Limit: max_steps_per_turn.
dims.providers: src/human/llm offers four protocol bases (openai, openai_responses, anthropic/anthropic_beta, google-genai incl. Vertex) with per-protocol typed traits, an MLIR-style message rewriter, and the rule 'no silent fallback'. Kimi is traits over the same bases plus an OAuth catalog. Supports models.dev import and Anthropic cache_control/OpenAI prompt_cache_key. Token usage is tracked; USD cost is not.
dims.tools: resolveExecution returns typed accesses, display and approvalRule before execution. A ToolScheduler runs non-conflicting file accesses in parallel; Bash and MCP tools default to 'all' and serialise. The pipeline is preflight, onBeforeExecuteTool (veto/waitUntil), schedule, onDidExecuteTool, then a 50k-char truncation with spill-to-disk output_path. About 30 built-ins.
dims.context: An 82-line system.md template. AGENTS.md is loaded from ~/.kimi-code, ~/.agents and every directory from git root to cwd, with path-triggered lazy injection; CLAUDE.md is not read. Compaction triggers at 0.85 or within 50k reserved and keeps 2k+20k user tokens plus the summary. A recovery footer points the model at its own wire.jsonl to grep old history.
dims.state: ~/.kimi-code/sessions/<workDirKey>/<id>/agents/<agentId>/wire.jsonl: append-only, versioned (protocol 1.5) with on-read migrations, branch edges via agent.switched records, fork, context.undo, ZIP export, corrupted-tail repair to .bak, and per-turn file-history blobs. In-flight turns are not replayed after a crash.
dims.safety: Modes manual, yolo, auto plus plan. A 13-policy first-match chain with tree-sitter-bash dangerous-command analysis, sensitive-file and .git guards, scoped allow/ask/deny rules, and git-cwd auto-approval of edits. Workspace trust gates project MCP. No OS sandbox and no network policy. Print mode forces auto. ACP mode labels invert the auto/yolo semantics.
dims.extensibility: Declarative plugins (kimi.plugin.json: skills, agents, mcpServers, hooks, commands) from a marketplace with official/curated tiers or from GitHub. 20 hook events using the Claude-Code-style exit-2/permissionDecision protocol. Skills in .kimi-code and .agents roots. CC/OpenCode-compatible agent files. MCP client over stdio/HTTP/SSE with OAuth. DI overrides require a fork.
dims.multi_agent: Agent tool: same-process subagents with their own wire, foreground or background, resume, context fork and per-call model; built-ins coder/explore/plan. AgentSwarm fans out to 128 subagents with a queue and concurrency cap. Goals and cron. Experimental Tower mode adds git-worktree missions, reviewer agents, rebase and a merge gate.
dims.surfaces: pi-tui TUI; kimi -p with text or stream-json; kimi acp (fork, list, resume, editor fs/terminal via scope shadowing); kimi web on kap-server (REST /api/v1 and v2, WS, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, experimental); a prebuilt web UI; VS Code extension; desktop launcher; kimi rc cloud relay; a private in-process node-sdk; single native binary.
dims.observability: First-party telemetry (typed track2 events, redaction, KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY). No OpenTelemetry. A per-request LLMRequestTrace is persisted in wire.jsonl. xstate inspection collector, vis session replay, and kimi-inspect over the /api/v1/debug DI reflection RPC. 183k LOC of engine tests; no eval harness in-tree.

builds_on: pi: packages/pi-tui is a vendored fork of earendil-works/pi packages/tui, pinned at upstream 53816d7 (v0.85.1+), with 19 intent cards in UPSTREAM.md; also uses @mariozechner/clipboard
kimi-cli-legacy: Python predecessor; packages/migration-legacy imports its ~/.kimi config, MCP and sessions
claude-code: compatible hook event names and exit-2/permissionDecision protocol, project .mcp.json, CC-style agent files, and an import-from-cc-codex skill
used_by: Zed and JetBrains IDEs via kimi acp
Kimi Code VS Code extension (apps/vscode, in-process via createKimiHarness)
Kimi Code desktop app and code-app web UI (via kap-server REST/WS)
Kimi Remote Control web client (code-rc.kimi.com relay)
key_insights: Parallel tool calls are ordered by declared ToolAccesses (file read/write/search with recursive prefixes) in a small conflict scheduler. Tools without declarations (Bash, MCP) default to 'all' and act as global barriers.

After compaction the model gets a footer with the absolute path and schema of its own append-only wire.jsonl plus grep/jq recipes. History is lossy in context but lossless on disk, which gives retrieval memory with no vector store.

Three harness generations are visible: Python kimi-cli, then a deleted TS 'v1' KimiCore engine, then agent-core-v2. Migration debris remains: a v1-shaped SDK facade, two provider registries, an unused maxRalphIterations key, and kosong surviving only as a name ('the kosong kernel is deleted' per the import linter).

Every engine/SDK package is private:true. The only published artifact is the CLI, so reuse means ACP, stream-json or the experimental HTTP API, or forking 280k LOC. Inside a fork, DI makes swapping any service a one-line overrideScopedService.

Headless kimi -p forbids --yolo/--auto but then forces 'auto' and bootstraps nonInteractive, which drops the dangerous-command policy. Only user deny rules and path guards remain, so CI needs external isolation.

In default manual mode, Write/Edit inside a git work tree is auto-approved on POSIX (git-cwd-write-approve), while sensitive files and .git paths still ask even in yolo. Git is treated as the undo mechanism.

ACP mode descriptions contradict the engine: ACP calls 'auto' 'safe operations' and 'yolo' 'everything', but auto approves everything while yolo still asks. ACP 'plan' claims no tool execution, yet Bash still runs under normal permissions.

Tower (experimental, flag-gated) is a deterministic multi-agent protocol: git-worktree missions, WIP snapshot commits, independent reviewer agents and a merge gate. Legacy KAOS's SSH remote backend and D-Mail checkpoint rewind did not survive the port.

features_notes.in_process_sdk: Private workspace SDK; vendoring required for direct engine reuse.
features_notes.worktrees: Tower orchestration is experimental and off by default.

records.name: Kimi CLI (legacy Python, archived)
records.one_liner: Moonshot's original Python terminal agent (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026): an imperative KimiSoul step loop over the kosong LLM layer and the PyKAOS local/SSH OS abstraction, with YAML agent specs, D-Mail checkpoint rewind, ACP, a --wire JSON-RPC mode and a FastAPI web UI. Superseded by Kimi Code CLI.

dims.loop: KimiSoul._agent_loop is an imperative per-step sequence: max-steps guard, then auto-compaction, then a context checkpoint, then _step() (kosong.step). A BackToTheFuture exception from D-Mail reverts to a checkpoint. Steers are consumed between steps. A 'Ralph' extra-iteration mode was configured by max_ralph_iterations.
dims.providers: Python kosong ChatProvider with kimi, openai_legacy, openai_responses, anthropic, google_genai/gemini and vertexai, plus _echo/_chaos test providers. kosong.step starts tool execution as each tool call streams in, overlapping tools with generation.
dims.tools: Toolsets loaded by Python import path from YAML agent specs (e.g. kimi_cli.tools.shell:Shell). Built-ins: Shell, ReadFile, WriteFile, StrReplaceFile, Glob, Grep, SearchWeb, FetchURL, SetTodoList, Task*, Agent, AskUserQuestion, plan tools, and optional SendDMail and Think. MCP via fastmcp. Tools run as asyncio tasks.
dims.context: system.md template args KIMI_AGENTS_MD, KIMI_SKILLS and KIMI_WORK_DIR_LS. AGENTS.md is merged from project root to work_dir. SimpleCompaction preserves the last 2 messages around an LLM summary. Dynamic injections. D-Mail lets the model fold context back to a CHECKPOINT n.
dims.state: ~/.kimi/sessions/<workdir>/<id>/context.jsonl (messages plus _checkpoint/_usage/_system_prompt lines) and wire.jsonl. Subagents are persisted under the session. Resume, fork (session_fork.py) and checkpoint revert are context-only; there is no file rewind.
dims.safety: ApprovalRuntime with approve, approve_for_session or reject; yolo and afk flags (afk implied by --print); per-session auto_approve_actions. No command analysis, no OS sandbox, no network policy.
dims.extensibility: 13 hook events (PreToolUse … Notification), plugin.json plugins in ~/.kimi/plugins, standard skills (/skill:) and flow skills (/flow:), MCP client management CLI, and YAML agent specs with extend and subagents.
dims.multi_agent: LaborMarket registers built-in subagent types coder/explore/plan. The Agent tool creates or resumes subagent instances persisted with their own wire/context. No swarm, worktrees or workflow engine.
dims.surfaces: prompt-toolkit/rich shell TUI; --print with text or stream-json; --acp and kimi acp (agent-client-protocol 0.8.0, ACPKaos routes IO to the editor); a --wire JSON-RPC stdio server; FastAPI web UI and vis; KimiCLI.create/run programmatic API; kosong, pykaos and kimi-sdk on PyPI.
dims.observability: Custom telemetry (track events, crash handlers), loguru logs, vis replay tool, tests_ai suite. No OpenTelemetry.

builds_on: codex: NOTICE credits Apache-2.0 OpenAI Codex code (skill-creator skill)
used_by: kimi-code: successor; packages/migration-legacy migrates its config, MCP, skills, plans, input history and sessions
key_insights: D-Mail (SendDMail plus the DenwaRenji checkpoint registry) let the model rewind its own context to an earlier CHECKPOINT and leave a note for its past self. It was context-only (no filesystem rewind), opt-in via the 'okabe' agent spec, and was not ported to the TS rewrite.
kosong.step began executing each tool as soon as its call finished streaming, overlapping tools with generation. The TS successor waits for llm.done and then schedules by access conflicts.

PyKAOS abstracted file and process operations behind a Kaos protocol with local and SSH backends, plus an ACPKaos that routed IO through the editor. The TS port kept the editor routing (acp-fs/acp-terminal) but dropped SSH.
The final commit short-circuits every entry point into an installer redirect to Kimi Code, and the repo is archived. The 'kimi-code' PyPI name is reserved as an empty archived stub.

checked_claims: Policy evaluation stops at the first matching rule
Noninteractive mode omits the dangerous-command policy
Auto approval precedes sensitive-file ask policies

corrections: Qualified absence and experimental worktree claims

corrections: Corrected default path guard: relative escapes denied, absolute outside-workspace paths allowed; sensitive-file checks vary by tool.
